translation.proposed_text_en:
If a wage-structuring provision within the meaning of Section 68(5) items 1 to 6 contains a special rule on the definition of the term “business trip,” that rule shall be applied. 
a) The mileage allowance shall be taken into account at most at the rates applicable to federal employees. 
b) The daily allowance for domestic business trips may amount to up to ATS 240 per day.
issues: The content of Section 68(5) items 1 to 6 is not supplied, so the exact class of qualifying wage-structuring provisions cannot be verified.

translation.proposed_text_en: If a more favourable provision on the charging of proportional daily allowances is contained in collective agreements or works agreements concluded on the basis of special collective agreement authorisations, or is based on service (salary) regulations of corporations under public law approved by the supervisory authority, it shall be taken into account. c) If, in the case of a domestic business trip, no higher costs for overnight accommodation are proven, an amount of up to 200 S may be taken into account as an overnight allowance including the cost of breakfast. d) Daily allowances for foreign business trips may be taken into account at the maximum rate of the foreign travel rates for federal employees. e) If, in the case of a foreign business trip, no higher costs for overnight accommodation— 152.
issues: The first sentence was minimally restructured so that collective or works agreements and approved public-law service regulations remain alternative bases for the favourable rule rather than one being contained in the other.
Item e is truncated before its consequence and cannot be translated or extracted as a complete rule.

translation.proposed_text_en:
(2) The taxpayer with limited tax liability shall submit a tax return for the domestic income of the preceding calendar year (assessment period) if  
1. the tax office requests the taxpayer to do so, or  
2. the domestic income consisted wholly or partly of income within the meaning of Section 2(3) numbers 1 to 3 and the profit had to be determined or has been determined on the basis of a comparison of business assets, or  
3. the total domestic income assessable to income tax pursuant to Section 102 has exceeded ATS 15,000.
issues: Changed 'expired calendar year' to the faithful and idiomatic 'preceding calendar year'.
The contents of Section 2(3) numbers 1 to 3 and Section 102 are not supplied.
